match_note: Nature Communications file (NCOMMS-26-002860-T; previously reviewed at another journal, those reports not included). Three referees in round 1 (R2's report was an attached file, quoted in full in the rebuttal); in round 2 R1, R2, R3 all recommend publication and 'Reviewer #4' is only an early-career co-reviewer note with no comments. Everything the referees point to is in v1: the Sci. Rep. 2022 and Bolle et al. citations, the para-2 statement that local imaging 'can be perturbative', Fig. 3 with non-overlapping 'Dataset 1'/'Dataset 2' and overlapping 22.5/24.0 mT labels, the '1-10 Hz bandwidth' force-noise estimate, the closing sentence on the single-photon strong-coupling regime, Fig. 1(c) caption without the red line explained, and no stated error-bar definition. One discrepancy: v1 says the two Fig. 3(a) runs were 'during the same cooldown', while the rebuttal says each Fig. 3 trace followed a separate thermal cycle; the rebuttal also changes the force-noise figure (v1: double-sided, 0.42-1.3 aN over 1-10 Hz; rebuttal: single-sided, 0.66 aN at ENBW 1 Hz).

concerns.quote: The overall study seems to be incremental to the previous work by the group Sci. Rep. 12, 1608 (2022).
concerns.summary: The work looks like an incremental extension of the group's 2022 paper, adding only finer field resolution that reveals the jumps.

concerns.quote: It should also be noted that Bolle et. al. (Nature, 1999) had made single-flux induced changes using micromechanical resonators as well.
concerns.summary: Mechanical detection of single-flux events with micromechanical resonators was already shown by Bolle et al. in 1999, undercutting novelty.

concerns.quote: Any misalignment in these three vectors, would mean that for each B_ip, B_oop needs to be tuned again. Therefore, it is important to mention the cross-coupling between the two magnetic fields.
concerns.summary: Misalignment between the SQUID loop and the in-plane and out-of-plane fields could cross-couple them, and the paper does not characterize this.

concerns.quote: it is not clear if the single-photon coupling rate or the flux-responsivity were maintained consistent for all values of B_ip.
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the coupling rate and flux responsivity stayed constant across in-plane fields, which could bias the extracted frequency.

concerns.quote: some relevant papers on integrating vortex-physics to cavity-electromechanics, and on the flux-coupled electromechanical devices have been overlooked
concerns.summary: Two relevant papers on vortex physics in cavity electromechanics and flux-coupled electromechanical devices are not cited.

concerns.quote: The critique of local imaging techniques should be augmented with the fact and it also gives the spatial information.
concerns.summary: The introduction's critique of local imaging methods should acknowledge that they provide spatial information.

concerns.quote: are the values of the fields at which the curves exhibit steps reproducible (whether they repeat without going through the thermal cycle).
concerns.summary: Fig. 3 datasets cover non-overlapping field ranges, so whether jump fields repeat within one cooldown is never shown.

concerns.quote: Generally, for the same device, I would expect vortices entering at the same fields. This is not what I see in Fig. 3.
concerns.summary: Jump fields differ between runs on the same device, and the paper does not discuss what changes after thermal cycling (for example a different pinning pattern).

concerns.quote: Generally, the discussion concerning Fig. 3 is too limited.
concerns.summary: The discussion of the key Fig. 3 data, including why the red and blue datasets span different fields, is too brief.

concerns.quote: it seems that the vortices enter more rarely than expected. One thing that was not clear about this part is whether the authors attribute each step to multiple vortices entering, or vortices with multiple flux quanta?
concerns.summary: Steps are sparser than the vortex-density estimate predicts, and it is unclear whether each step means several vortices or multi-quanta vortices.

concerns.quote: The authors then show the force sensitivity over a 1-10 Hz bandwidth. Why was this bandwidth range chosen? Is this the actual averaging time used in the experiments?
concerns.summary: The force-sensitivity benchmark uses an unexplained 1-10 Hz bandwidth that may not match the actual measurement.

concerns.quote: Do the authors have a reason for not driving the oscillator? If not, I believe this could greatly increase the sensitivity of the experiment.
concerns.summary: Coherently driving the resonator (FM/PLL tracking) would likely improve frequency resolution, and the choice of passive thermal readout is not justified.

concerns.quote: Could the authors in principle localize the vortices by looking at the frequency shift of multiple modes, similar to that done in mass sensing experiments? I think this aspect could be worth commenting on.
concerns.summary: The paper should comment on whether multimode frequency shifts could localize vortices along the string.

concerns.quote: the authors claim that their work provide guidance for architectures in the single photon strong coupling regime... I would like the authors to be more explicit.
concerns.summary: The closing claim of guidance for single-photon strong-coupling architectures is vague.

concerns.quote: the authors do not describe how these error bars are obtained, nor precisely what they mean (1 sd? 68%confidence interval?).
concerns.summary: Error bars are shown without saying how they were obtained or what interval they represent.

concerns.quote: Fig 1c: The red line is not explained in the caption.
concerns.summary: The Fig. 1(c) caption does not explain the red line.

concerns.quote: Fig 2b: This figure would be much more legible if the authors subtract Ω0 from the x-axis and labelled 3 axis ticks
concerns.summary: Fig. 2(b) would be more legible with a frequency-offset axis and labelled ticks.

concerns.quote: In Fig 3 the labels for 22.5 and 24.0 mT are slightly overlapping.
concerns.summary: Two field labels in Fig. 3 overlap.

first_round.quote: While the physics presented in the study is interesting and I enjoyed reading it, I find it rather difficult to recommend its publication in Nature Communications
I therefore recommend that the paper should be accepted to Nature Communications after considering the comments below.
I think it should be published in Nature Communications. I still have suggestions for improvements, which I would like to be addressed before the paper is accepted.

recommendations.note: The file states the manuscript was previously reviewed at another journal; only Nature Communications versions are included, so Version 0 here is treated as the first round. R1 is inferred as reject because R1 judges the work incremental relative to Sci. Rep. 2022 and Bolle et al. 1999, and also raises technical and citation points. R2's first-round report was only an attached file ('See attached file'), so R2's wording is taken from the passages quoted in the authors' rebuttal. R2's requests are clarifications, explanations and figure fixes, hence minor revision. R3 asks for an expanded discussion of Fig. 3 but recommends publication, hence minor revision. R4 appears only in Version 1, as an early-career co-reviewer of one of the listed reviewers' reports; the file does not say which one. R4 therefore has no separate first-round report and cannot be assigned a recommendation, so R4 is omitted from the list.
recommendations.label: contested
